subject: Urgent: kernel scheduling throttle — mitigation checklist & customer note request
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Urgent: kernel scheduling throttle — mitigation checklist & customer note request

Team — we started getting alert noise at 09:05 indicating a burst in p95 latency (text-gen) and a simultaneous drop in overall throughput for the hosted gen-api fleet serving SaaSCo. Dashboard: p95 jumped from ~220ms to ~1.3s, and effective req/s dropped ~28% for the affected shard pool.

Initial ask: I need an internal triage summary and an immediate mitigation checklist we can run (low-risk steps first) plus a short customer-facing note I can send to SaaSCo (CC: EngOps). Priority: limit blast radius and give the customer projection + ETA to stabilize.

Observed so far:
- Alerts triggered from metric service and user-reported slowdowns (SaaSCo Slack thread).
- Affected instances are mostly on the m4-dense pool in us-west-2, same auto-scale group.
- No recent deployment in the last 4 hours.

Attach anything you collect (profiles, lsof, dmesg snapshots). I attached a live cpu snapshot I pulled.

Ben
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 10:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: kernel scheduling throttle — mitigation checklist & customer note request

Ben — quick triage notes (still digging):
- Correlation looks strongest with kernel scheduler stalls on the hypervisor layer (we see elevated steal% and uneven scheduling latency across the pool). Sampling shows heavy kernel preemption near GPU DMA windows which lines up with a vendor kernel microcode path that got triggered by a background maintenance job on a subset of hosts.
- Model runtime itself (inference process) shows normal latencies when isolated on a warm host; the spike is host-level scheduling.

Immediate mitigations I recommend (ordered by risk):
1) Route traffic away from affected auto-scale group via weight shift (5–10% per minute) — low risk.
2) Temporarily enable fallback model variant (smaller, quantized) for the highest throughput routes while we stabilize — requires PM approval.
3) Evacuate and replace the most impacted hosts (drain + reprovision) — medium risk, expected recovery in ~20–30m for drained hosts.
4) If we need a faster stopgap, start a short-lived secondary fleet on a different instance family + move canary traffic — costs spike but rapid.

I attached the live-cpu-snapshot and will push a runbook diff for the cgroup tweak we're testing. Give me 15–30m and I can supply a concise 3-bullet customer note we can use.

— Marissa
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: kernel scheduling throttle — mitigation checklist & customer note request

Thanks Marissa. Good color.
Operational asks:
- Dylan/Hannah: can SRE execute (1) weight-shift + (3) drain-replace cadence now? Prioritize minimal customer disruption. Call out risks we should include in the customer note.
- Marissa: please produce the 3-bullet customer note + one-sentence root-cause summary we can share externally. Keep it non-technical but transparent.
- I'll coordinate with SaaSCo and request they throttle non-critical traffic while we stabilize.

Target timeline: weight-shift started within 10m, drain cycle started within 25m, and a draft customer message in 30m. If we need the secondary fleet (4) I authorize it.

Ben
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 11:25:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Urgent: kernel scheduling throttle — mitigation checklist & customer note request

We started weight-shift at 11:18 (5% every 2m). Early telemetry shows p95 coming down on the fastest routes (~400–500ms).
Actions underway / notes:
- Draining the 6 most impacted hosts now; expected to finish 11:50–12:00.
- Applying cgroup soft-affinity to inference processes on remaining hosts as a stopgap (runbook patch applied) — low risk, no restart required. Patch attached as runbook-patch-v1.diff.
- Starting a small secondary fleet (n=8 instances, alternate family) as warm standby; not shifting production traffic to it yet.

Risks: brief throttling during drain if connections are sticky; we'll disable keep-alive on the affected route briefly to accelerate redistribution.

I'll post a short internal runbook summary once drains are complete.

— Dylan
From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
To: Charles Meyer <charles.meyer@saasco.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Dylan Brooks <dylan_brooks@redwood.ai>, Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.ai>, SaaSCo Eng Ops <engops@saasco.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Brief update: transient performance impact for some gen routes

Charles — quick update from Redwood: we detected a transient performance impact affecting some of the text-generation routes used by SaaSCo earlier today. Our engineers identified host-level CPU scheduling interference on a subset of instances and have already taken steps to reduce impact.

What we did so far:
- Shifted traffic off the affected hosts and are draining/replacing them.
- Applied a configuration patch to reduce host scheduler interference for inference processes.
- Brought a small standby fleet online to absorb traffic if required.

What to expect now:
- Most affected routes should see improved latency in the next 30–60 minutes.
- We’ll follow up with a short post-incident note that includes the root cause and preventative steps.

If you see continued issues after 13:30 PT, please reply and we’ll prioritize an immediate rollback and deeper investigation. Apologies for the disruption — we’re on it.

Ben Carter
Enterprise Success Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Charles Meyer <charles.meyer@saasco.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.ai>
Cc: SaaSCo Eng Ops <engops@saasco.com>
Date: Tue, 3 Aug 2027 16:43:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Brief update: transient performance impact for some gen routes

Thanks Ben — we saw improvement around 12:20 and traffic looks stable. Appreciate the quick response and the clear updates. Please do share the post-incident summary when available; our leadership will want the RCA and the plan to prevent recurrence.

— Charles
